_README: Routing for this project: which kind of work goes to which model or worker. CLAUDE.md points here instead of carrying a table, so this is the one place to change the split. Copy it to .claude/routing.json in every project; edit values per project, keep the shape. Nothing parses it - the agent reads it before the first delegation of a session - so every string is written for a reader. The model of a subagent role is authoritative in the role's agents/<name>.md frontmatter; no role pins effort - every subagent runs at the harness default for its model. This file names the role and repeats the model for orientation only.

conserve.rule: Only the lead session is worth saving. Everything the lead reads is re-sent on every later turn, so the routing question is never 'where is this cheapest' but 'what must never enter the lead's context'. Subagents, GLM and agy are spent freely when that keeps the lead's window small and the result verifiable.
conserve.quota_price_note: Most expensive first. Anthropic carries the lead and every Claude subagent; Z.AI carries GLM; Google AI Pro carries agy and refills every five hours.

axes._note: Two mechanisms that look alike and are not interchangeable. A subagent is started with the Agent tool and picks a model from the harness enum; it can receive the lead's context in its prompt and runs in parallel with others. A worker is a separate process reached through a wrapper in Bash; it starts blank on every call, cannot be talked to, and returns one answer. GLM has no subagent form - model: 'glm' matches nothing. agy has no subagent form either. Haiku 4.5 is below the model floor and its alias is the harness's reserved slot, see 'reserved'; Haiku 5.5 becomes pickable when it ships.

model_policy.floor: Anthropic models of generation 5.1 and later only: Fable 5.1 (alias fable, claude-fable-5-1) and Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5). Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 are not used.
model_policy.on_release: Sonnet 5.5: agy-driver, implementer, sweeper and drafter move to it. Haiku 5.5: assignable for the cheapest mechanical work (sweeper, drafter). Update the role frontmatter, this file and the three model-table-rev copies together.
model_policy.effort: no role pins effort; every subagent runs at the harness default for its model (Fable 5.1 high, Opus 5.5 medium). Workflow agent() calls leave effort unset too.
model_policy.ids: full ids in frontmatter where an alias could resolve below the floor - the opus alias may still mean Opus 5.

tiers._note: Three tiers for executable work. The lead never calls a worker itself; a driver subagent does, and only the driver's short report reaches the lead.
tiers.lead: designs, plans, writes the brief for a driver, accepts or rejects the result
tiers.driver: a subagent that owns one delegated task end to end: writes the worker brief, calls the wrapper, runs the check, re-briefs on failure, commits or reverts, reports in a few lines
tiers.worker: GLM or agy, one self-contained job per call

lead.covers: design, plans, briefs for drivers and subagents, consolidation, final acceptance
lead.model_is_parameter: set per project; claude-opus-5-5 where Fable is unavailable or the project runs in fast mode. Drivers stay separate subagents whichever model leads - the point of the tier is context isolation, not a different head.

glm_driver.covers: every self-contained execution task that goes to GLM: implementing an approved plan, a sweep or audit of a module, a long draft, a mechanical multi-file pass
glm_driver.why_opus: the driver decides whether a result is acceptable or needs a re-brief; that is judgement, not mechanics, and it is the last check before the lead sees anything

loop.on_pass: commit `wip(<scope>): ...` on the current branch (`master` in this repository)
loop.on_fail: `git checkout .`, then a new brief that names the concrete failure - never the same brief again
loop.verification: the driver runs the project's check command itself; the worker is told not to run it and not to claim it passed
loop.after_limit: stop and report, even if the last attempt was close

glm_driver.report_to_lead: one line per item, nothing else: what was done, the check command and its last line, what failed and why, worker calls and tokens spent, commit hash. No diff, no retelling of the worker's answer.

execution_worker.covers: the execution itself, under a glm-driver
requirements: the task is self-contained and ends in a commit
there is a mechanical acceptance check - a command that must pass
the working directory is a clean git checkout (the wrapper refuses otherwise)
execution_worker.shell: off by default; the driver passes --allow-shell only when the task itself needs a terminal (fixtures, a migration, a generator) and says so in its report
execution_worker.invoke: python C:/Users/cupik/.claude/bin/glm-run.py, from the driver, never from the lead

in_flight_execution.covers: a step inside the lead's current work: a one- or two-file edit, a check that needs the context the lead is holding, work on a dirty tree that is inconvenient to commit mid-way, work outside a git repository, small parallel probes
in_flight_execution.model_note: Sonnet 5 is below the floor; these roles move to Sonnet 5.5 when it ships, and sweeper and drafter are candidates for Haiku 5.5
in_flight_execution.why_not_glm: GLM starts blank and needs a clean tree; these tasks need neither the ceremony nor the isolation

artifact.covers: work whose deliverable is a file or folder produced from scratch: a research report with web search, a long standalone document, a generated module, anything matching one of agy's own skills
artifact.boundary: agy never edits the project's working tree. Its --dir is a side directory the driver prepares (a fresh git repository with the inputs copied in and committed, since the wrapper requires a clean git checkout). The driver checks that the artifact exists on disk and returns its path with a short report; bringing it into the project is the lead's decision, made as an ordinary edit.
artifact.acceptance: the lead spot-checks three cited claims against their sources before bringing a research artifact in
artifact.why_this_model: the driver has nothing to judge here - it prepares the side directory, calls at most twice (one retry after a fixable failure), and relays a path; claude-opus-5-5 is the cheapest model above the floor

verify.covers: cross-model adversarial re-check of a finding produced by a different model, only when a finding is contested or a report goes to a human; never a re-check of the caller's own work
verify.constraint: never the model that produced the thing being checked; for a finding written by fable, call with model: claude-opus-5-5
verify.note: not run on every delegation. A glm-driver's check is verification enough for routine execution; the lead reads the diff when it decides to.

review.finding_stage: the reviewer reports every issue including uncertain and low-severity ones, with confidence and severity per finding; filtering happens in the verify stage, never in the finding stage

research.covers: a question that must be answered from a primary source: a library's current API, a spec, a documented tool behaviour
research.why_not_agy: agy is for a research deliverable (a report to keep); a researcher answers a question the lead needs now

choose._note: Walk down in order; the first match decides.
choose.1: one lookup, one file, one edit, or a step that needs this session's context -> the lead does it
choose.2: the deliverable is an artifact produced from scratch, or the task matches one of agy's own skills -> artifact (agy-driver -> agy)
choose.3: self-contained, ends in a commit, has a check command, clean git checkout available -> execution_worker (glm-driver -> GLM)
choose.4: many files to read, one conclusion to return -> sweeper
choose.5: a section of a long deliverable from settled material -> drafter
choose.6: an in-flight code step that does not meet 3 -> implementer
choose.7: a finding to challenge -> verify; a diff to review -> review; a fact to look up in a primary source -> research

parallel.rule: Two GLM calls in one checkout collide: the second refuses on the first's dirty tree, or the drivers revert each other. Run parallel glm-drivers only with `isolation: worktree` in the Agent tool, one worktree and one branch per driver; the lead merges afterwards. Inside one checkout, one driver at a time.
parallel.ceiling: the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_* subagent variables in the project environment (not in Claude Code's documentation - check them against the current binary), plus the SDK's max_budget_usd

glm.what: Claude Code itself, started as a child process on the Z.AI endpoint. It reads this project's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md on its own, so the brief does not restate the contract.
glm.installed_copy: ~/.claude/bin/glm-run.py - what the permission entry names and what runs
glm.source: glm-agy-cc-proxy/GLM/glm-run.py, the versioned original; after editing it, copy it over the installed copy
glm.permission_entry: Bash(python C:/Users/cupik/.claude/bin/glm-run.py:*) in ~/.claude/settings.json, matched against the command text, so spell it exactly
glm.skill: glm - ~/.claude/skills/glm is a junction to .claude/skills/glm/ in glm-agy-cc-proxy; edit it there
glm.cost_detail_large_task: 31 900 input + 264 800 cache-read + 17 500 output, 23 turns, 263 s, no shell. A nine-file, 210-line Python package: add a second input format to the parser, a section to the report, and tests for both. Seven files edited and one added, 14 tests to 33, every one passing on the first attempt. This is the figure to judge a delegation against.
glm.cost_caveat: total_cost_usd in the wrapper's report is not a Z.AI charge - Claude Code prices it from a table with no GLM entry. Compare calls by tokens.

limits_observed._note: measured on the first real glm-driver run, 2026-09-15
limits_observed.no_edits_under_dot_claude: the worker's Edit/Write calls on paths under .claude/ (a skill file in the project) were permission-denied under the default acceptEdits posture. The driver makes those edits itself after the call; do not re-brief the worker for them.
limits_observed.timeout_for_multi_file: a task touching eight files with a 641-line rewrite hit a 25-minute timeout on the first call and finished on the second (31 turns, 245 s). Split such a task, or set --timeout-min 40 and accept the wait.

agy.what: Google's Antigravity CLI, a separate agent with its own tools and skills, on a personal Google AI Pro account.
agy.installed_copy: ~/.claude/bin/agy-run.py - what the permission entry names and what runs
agy.source: glm-agy-cc-proxy/AGY/agy-run.py, the versioned original; after editing it, copy it over the installed copy
agy.quota: personal Google AI Pro, refills every five hours
agy.availability_note: An account, eligibility or region error from agy ('account is not eligible for Antigravity ... not available in your location') can be transient and costs no quota. The driver retries once and reports both outcomes as the first line of its report; the lead passes it to the human before doing anything else (AGENTS.md, 'Escalate to a human'). Rerouting the artifact work to a researcher or drafter subagent is the human's call, not the driver's.
agy.skill: agy - ~/.claude/skills/agy is a junction to .claude/skills/agy/ in glm-agy-cc-proxy; edit it there

cost_tokens._note: input tokens only, measured 2026-09-13; with cache-read the large task is ~691 000 (GLM's figures above include cache-read)

agy.brief_leaves_the_machine: the brief goes to a personal Google account; AGENTS.md rule 3 applies to it. The same is true of GLM and Z.AI.

haiku.assignable: false until Haiku 5.5 ships; Haiku 4.5 is below the 5.1 floor
haiku.what: the harness's own service slot - auto mode's command-safety classifier, and similar background calls
haiku.leave_as_installed: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL keeps the harness's own default; it is set by the installation, not by a routing decision
haiku.why: when that slot names a model the session cannot reach, running commands stops working while file reads carry on. The session holding the bad value cannot fix itself, because settings are read once at startup.

unverified.glm_vs_opus: GLM holds the execution slot by decision, not by measurement - nothing here has benchmarked GLM against Opus 5.5 on the same task. Replace this entry with a number the day someone does.
unverified.driver_loop_limit: three worker calls per task is a starting value, not a measured optimum.
